theme: The song of Moses, covenant lawsuit in poetry
readingInstruction: Read Deuteronomy 31:30-32:52. This is the Song of Moses, a long poem that serves as a witness to Israel. Read it aloud if you can, and notice how it moves from praise to accusation to comfort.
settingTheScene: God has told Moses to write a song and teach it to Israel, so that it will be a witness against them when they turn away. The song is placed after the last of Moses’ sermons. It is a poem in the form of a covenant lawsuit: it summons heaven and earth as witnesses, states God’s faithfulness, charges Israel with unfaithfulness, announces judgment, and ends with a promise of vindication. After the song, God tells Moses to go up Mount Nebo and die.
observation: “Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak, and let the earth hear the words of my mouth” (32:1).
“The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice. A God of faithfulness and without iniquity, just and upright is he” (32:4).
“They have dealt corruptly with him; they are no longer his children because they are blemished” (32:5).
“Is not he your father, who created you, who made you and established you?” (32:6).
“The LORD’s portion is his people, Jacob his allotted heritage” (32:9). He found him in a desert land… “he encircled him, he cared for him, he kept him as the apple of his eye” (32:10).
“Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, that flutters over its young, spreading out its wings, catching them, bearing them on its pinions” (32:11).
“But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked… He forsook God who made him and scoffed at the Rock of his salvation” (32:15).
“See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god beside me; I kill and I make alive… and there is none that can deliver out of my hand” (32:39).
interpretation:
The song is a retelling of Israel’s story in miniature. God is the Rock, perfect and faithful. He found Israel in the wilderness, protected them like the apple of his eye, and carried them like an eagle carries its young. They grew fat in the land and forsook him. It is the same pattern you have seen throughout the wilderness story: grace, prosperity, rebellion, judgment.

The image of the eagle is beautiful. An eagle stirs up its nest so the young must fly, and then hovers beneath them, ready to catch them. It is a picture of God’s care that is both challenging and protective. He pushes his people out of comfort, and he does not let them fall.

The word “Rock” appears repeatedly. It is a name for God that stresses his stability and strength. Everything else in the song shifts, but the Rock does not. The nations’ gods are not rocks: “Their rock is not like our Rock” (32:31). In a world of change and disappointment, there is a foundation.

The accusation is heavy. Israel is called “a crooked and twisted generation” (32:5). The children have turned away from their father. This is a covenant lawsuit, with heaven and earth as the jury. But the sentence is not final. Verse 36 says, “The LORD will vindicate his people and have compassion on his servants.” The song moves from judgment to compassion. God’s last word is not wrath.

The final verses of the chapter return to Moses himself. He is told to go up Mount Nebo, look at the land, and die. He will not enter, “because you broke faith with me.” His own failure at Meribah has consequences. But the great leader receives a view of the land and a peaceful death, a last gift.
connection: Paul quotes the song in Romans 10:19 and 12:19, and 15:10, and in 1 Corinthians 10:22. Jesus compared himself to a hen gathering her chicks, and in the parable of the wicked tenants he spoke of the vineyard owner’s son, echoing Israel’s rejection. Revelation 15:3 says that the redeemed sing “the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb.” The Rock is Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4), and the foundation on which we build (Matthew 7:24-25).
application:
Read the song aloud once through. Notice which phrase speaks to you.

Ask whether you have grown “fat and kicked” in a season of ease. Return to the Rock.

Thank God for the image of the eagle, and for the ways he has both pushed and caught you.
prayerPrompts: Praise God as the Rock whose work is perfect.
Confess where you have forgotten the Rock of your salvation.
Ask him to vindicate his people and have compassion on them.
